newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to keep all Ruiz Massieu money, judge says.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to keep all Ruiz Massieu money, judge says.

text.p: A federal judge has ruled that the U.S. government is entitled to keep all $9 million it seized from a Texas bank account once held by former Mexican deputy attorney general Mario Ruiz Massieu because the money came from drug-trafficker bribes.
The decision, unveiled in court documents on Monday, reverses a March jury verdict in which Ruiz Massieu was allowed to retain $1.1 million of the cash.

U.S. District Judge Nancy Atlas, who presided over the March trial, said the jury found that Ruiz Massieu got the money from drug-traffickers seeking protection for their operations and therefore he had to forfeit all of it.
She said there was no proof that any of the money had come from Ruiz Massieu's family or from large bonuses paid by the Mexican government, as he claimed in court.

"The court finds that claimant's (Ruiz Massieu) evidence is unsubstantiated and not credible," Atlas said. She said the jury apparently awarded Ruiz Massieu $1.1 million on the basis of testimony by his father that he had given his son that amount for safekeeping.

Further, Atlas said federal prosecutors proved in the week-long trial that Ruiz Massieu was part of a massive drug-trafficking conspiracy that "included certain officials within the PGR (Mexican Attorney General's office) ... and other named and unnamed officials working within the Mexican Federal Judicial Police."
Co-conspirators, Atlas said, included drug-traffickers Juan Garcia Abrego, the Arellano Felix brothers, and Amado Carrillo Fuentes.

Ruiz Massieu was arrested in the United States in March 1995 when he left Mexico amid charges he had covered up for the alleged murderers of his brother, a former top ruling party official, and had embezzled money. His brother, Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, then head of Mexico's ruling political party, was gunned down in downtown Mexico City in September 1994.

Prosecutors here charged that Mario Ruiz Massieu took millions of dollars in bribes from drug-traffickers while he was supposedly a leading drug fighter in the Mexican attorney general's office starting in 1990. They seized the Texas bank account two years ago on grounds that it came from illegal sources.

Ruiz Massieu, who could still appeal Atlas' decision, faces hearings to deport him back to Mexico next month in New Jersey. Also, news reports here said he is under grand jury investigation for allegedly laundering drug money.
